title: Scamming a Car Warranty Scammer
summary: A creator strings along a car warranty telemarketer posing as calling on Ford's behalf, exposing scripted lies about affiliation and pricing and the thin fine print behind the pitch.

assertions.quote: I work on behalf of Ford Motor company and they chose you directly to get this deal
if something happens to your car doing normal wear and tear incorrect fluids accidental damage or just plain old misuse you can't get it covered

verdicts.note: Vehicle service contracts do exclude wear-and-tear and misuse like most warranties, but 'everything isn't covered' overstates how little legitimate contracts actually cover for genuine mechanical breakdowns.

assertions.quote: you'd have to get everything pre-approved by the company so you can't just show up to a repair shop
most States sell your data and if you don't believe me look it up States like California North and South Carolina Florida are making millions

verdicts.note: State DMVs do sell driver and vehicle data under permitted-use exceptions, and data brokers separately aggregate and resell contact information, feeding these call lists.

assertions.quote: we have the highest level claim payout in the industry it's fifteen thousand dollars no questions asked

verdicts.note: Legitimate contracts require documentation and often pre-approval, so a 'no questions asked' guarantee is a known red-flag phrase in scam scripts.

assertions.quote: the hundred dollars is a refundable deposit today because it's a live policy

verdicts.note: Requiring card details before full disclosure is a common tactic some legitimate sellers use too, but it's exploited by scam operations to lock in commitment before disclosure.

FTC confirms scam sellers "pressure you to give them personal financial information and a down payment right away, before they give you details about the service contract" -- matching the sequence (payment/card info before contract details) though not the "refundable deposit" framing specifically.
